source.citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form, Ch. XIII 'The Shapes of Horns, and of Teeth or Tusks: with a Note on Torsion', pp. 612-634, Figs. 318-324

key_pages.619: verbal statement of the differential-growth law (equal rates -> straight; unequal -> curved; constant ratio -> logarithmic spiral; non-diametral max/min -> helical component)
key_pages.618: cardboard-triangle stacking experiment, Ovis ammon edge lengths 80:74:45 cm ~ 9:8:5
key_pages.621-623: St Venant torsion: circular section unwarped; triangular prism warped into anticlastic surface, Fig. 321 contours, Fig. 322 clay-cast contours
key_pages.632-634: nail, claw, beak, tooth follow the log spiral; rodent incisor; elephant/mammoth tusk tip ~ pole; Mastodon low angle vs mammoth high; long tusks (mammoth, Babirussa) are curves of double curvature

claim_text: Teeth and tusks grow by the same spiral/torsion geometry (with St Venant torsion curves describing the twisted prismatic forms).

claim_decomposition.C1_log_spiral_tusk: A tooth/tusk elongating by basal accretion with a constant ratio of growth rates on opposite sides and a gnomonically widening section is a logarithmic (equiangular) spiral whose tip lies near the pole (pp. 632-634).
claim_decomposition.C2_accretion_curvature_law: Curvature is produced by the summed small differences of growth rate on the two sides (p. 633), i.e. kappa = (v_max - v_min) / (w * v_mean); with constant section (rodent incisor) this is a circle (psi = 90 deg limit), with gnomonic widening a log spiral.
claim_decomposition.C3_double_curvature_twist: Very long tusks (mammoth, Babirussa) acquire a helical component ('curve of double curvature, like a twisted horn') from slight lateral asymmetry / torsional strain (p. 634, pp. 617-622).
claim_decomposition.C4_st_venant_torsion_curves: The twisted prismatic (trihedral) form is described by St Venant's torsion theory: a circular cylinder twists without warping; a non-circular prism warps each section into an anticlastic surface whose contour lines (Fig. 321) make the sinuous growth lines on each face half convex / half concave (pp. 621-623).

E1_equiangular_spiral.formula: r(theta) = r0 * exp(k * theta),  k = cot(psi)

variables.r: radius vector from the spiral pole
variables.psi: constant angle between radius vector and tangent (Thompson's 'spiral angle')

E1_equiangular_spiral.source: Thompson Ch. XI (eqn of the equiangular spiral) applied in Ch. XIII pp. 616-617, 633-634

E2_whorl_expansion.formula: W = r(theta + 2 pi) / r(theta) = exp(2 pi k)

E3_curvature_of_log_spiral.formula: rho_c = r * sqrt(1 + k^2) = r / sin(psi);  kappa = sin(psi) / r
E3_curvature_of_log_spiral.source: standard property used implicitly in Thompson's pole construction (p. 634)

E4_differential_accretion_curvature.formula: kappa = (v_max - v_min) / (w * v_mean) = Delta / w,   Delta = 2 (1 - lambda) / (1 + lambda),   lambda = v_min / v_max

variables.v_max, v_min: longitudinal growth rates on the convex and concave sides of the basal growth zone
variables.w: width of the section across the growth gradient

E4_differential_accretion_curvature.source: Thompson pp. 612, 619, 633 (verbal); algebraic form reconstructed in this loop

E5_gnomonic_closure.formula: w = c_r r  =>  sin(psi) = Delta / c_r ;  equivalently w = c_s s (arc-length taper, s = r / cos psi)  =>  tan(psi) = Delta / c_s,  c_r = c_s / cos(psi);   w = const  =>  circle of radius R = w / Delta

variables.c_r: taper ratio section width / radius vector
variables.c_s: taper ratio section width / arc length from the tip (what a photograph measures)

E5_gnomonic_closure.source: combination of E3 and E4; Thompson's circle/spiral dichotomy for incisor vs tusk (pp. 633-634)

E6_screw_accretion_helix.formula: per unit arc length the body frame rotates by Omega = kappa * b + tau * n;  constant (kappa, tau) => circular helix; with gnomonic scaling => conical log helico-spiral

variables.b: in-section bending axis perpendicular to the growth gradient
variables.tau: twist rate from oblique fibre growth / torsional strain

E6_screw_accretion_helix.source: Thompson pp. 617-620 ('a plane logarithmic spiral with a helical spiral in space superposed'; 'shear' component)

E7_uniform_torsion_helix_angle.formula: tan(phi) = rho * tau (phi = fibre inclination from the axis);  pitch P = 2 pi / tau;  Kiladze ratio tan(alpha) = BC/AC = P / (2 d) = pi / (tau d)

variables.rho: radial distance of the surface fibre
variables.alpha: inclination of the spiral arc from the transverse plane as defined by Kiladze & Chernova (2018)

E7_uniform_torsion_helix_angle.source: St Venant (1856) torsion kinematics; Kiladze & Chernova (2018) Fig. 1 definition

E8_st_venant_warping_triangle.formula: u_z(x, y) = (tau / (2 a)) * (3 x^2 y - y^3)   (equilateral prism, centroid at O, vertex on +x; nodal lines y = 0 and y = +/- sqrt(3) x)

variables.a: side-related length in Thompson's Fig. 321 (OX = 2a/3, side at x = -a/3)

E9_st_venant_warping_ellipse.formula: u_z(x, y) = tau * (b^2 - a^2) / (a^2 + b^2) * x * y;  circular section a = b => u_z = 0
E9_st_venant_warping_ellipse.source: St Venant (1856); Thompson p. 622 ('a twist leaves each circular section unchanged')

boundary_and_initial_conditions.tusk: tip near the pole (Thompson: 'assume the tip actually coincides with the pole'), r(theta_tip) = r_tip -> small; basal growth zone adds material at theta_base; tusk is the arc theta in [theta_tip, theta_base]
boundary_and_initial_conditions.incisor: constant section width w; worn anteriorly as fast as added posteriorly; visible arc is a circular segment
boundary_and_initial_conditions.narwhal_torsion: straight axis (kappa ~ 0), uniform twist rate tau along the visible shaft, surface fibres/grooves start at the alveolus and run to the tip
boundary_and_initial_conditions.prism_warping: stress-free lateral faces (Neumann condition for the warping function), rigid-body rotation of each section by tau z about the centroid

spiral_angle_psi_deg_thompson.Mammoth / existing elephants tusk: high (same angle, differing in size only)

sweep_used_in_script.taper_c_note: taper c in the script is the arc-length taper c_s (px of width per px of arc)

empirical_claims_to_test.test: segmented mammoth-tusk centreline: OLS fit ln r = ln r0 + k theta about a grid-refined pole; Pearson r, RMSE; compared with a constant-curvature circle (psi = 90 deg) null
empirical_claims_to_test.prediction_if_true: r_log > r_circle and kappa decreasing monotonically from tip to base

empirical_claims_to_test.test: kappa(s) * w(s) along the tusk; CV(kappa w) vs CV(kappa)
empirical_claims_to_test.prediction_if_true: CV(kappa w) < CV(kappa): curvature scales inversely with local width as the accretion law requires

empirical_claims_to_test.test: narwhal groove inclination by structure tensor in the low-foreshortening central strip; converted to Kiladze tan(alpha) = pi / (2 tan phi); z-score vs 66.88 +/- 3.34 deg (SD = SEM * sqrt(30)); sign of d(tan alpha)/d(1/d) along the shaft (uniform-tau St Venant prediction: positive)
numerical St Venant warping u_z for the equilateral prism; count sign sectors around the centroid and sign changes per face; overlay Thompson Fig. 321
empirical_claims_to_test.prediction_if_true: 6 alternating sectors, exactly 1 sign change per face at its midpoint

does_not_claim: 3-D double curvature of the mammoth tusk cannot be measured from a single 2-D photograph
no CT or growth-rate (v_max, v_min) data: lambda is inferred, not measured
narwhal is a torsion analogue, not a Thompson-named specimen
